question: The presence of dysmorphic red blood cells (acanthocytes) and/or red cell casts on urine microscopy indicates glomerular haematuria, whereas isomorphic red cells suggest a non-glomerular (urological) source.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. Urine microscopy morphology is the cornerstone of haematuria classification: dysmorphic RBCs/RBC casts = glomerular origin; isomorphic RBCs = non-glomerular (urological) origin. Urine colour alone cannot make this distinction.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Red cells passing through damaged glomerular capillary walls are deformed by osmotic and mechanical forces, producing dysmorphic RBCs and casts. Isomorphic RBCs come from the urothelial surface and indicate a urological (non-glomerular) source such as calculi, trauma, or tumour.
